message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 170, "amount_cents": 17127}, {"order_id": 172, "amount_cents": 7535}, {"order_id": 175, "amount_cents": 2957}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Start by listing orders and refunds so I can check the handoff before using net_balance for each customer.
Next I need the refunds list to cross-check W2's handoff claims against the actual refund records before paying anyone.
The refund list matches W2's handoff exactly (orders 170, 172, 175). Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
I checked acme by hand: orders 170 and 173 total 28386, less refund 170 (17127), gives 11259, which matches net_balance. Recording the acme payout now.
Acme's payout is recorded and matches my hand check. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance, since birch has no refunds in the list.
Birch has no refunds, so its order total should equal the net balance. Orders 171 and 174 sum to 18633, which matches net_balance. Recording the birch payout.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance before recording anything.
Cobalt's orders 172 and 175 total 64994, less refunds 7535 and 2957 (10492), giving 54502, which matches net_balance. Recording the cobalt payout.
All three customers have been paid and each recorded amount matched its hand-checked total from the order and refund records. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
